Subject: Hybrid on-prem egress & shared-services architecture review (control plane / data plane)

Hi Samir / Maya —

Thanks for agreeing to look at Atlas Retail's private deployment. Attached are two artifacts: a high-level hybrid VPC diagram (redwood_hybrid_vpc_egress_v1.drawio.png) and a control-plane/data-plane flow PDF (redwood_controlplane_dataflow_v1.pdf). We want to validate the following constraints with your network/security teams:

- Control plane: persistent TLS tunnel from customer VPCs to Redwood control plane in our managed region (mutual TLS, cert pinning), limited to a small set of IPs.
- Data plane: inference GPUs remain in-customer (on-prem VPCs) with egress constrained to customer's central proxy cluster for DLP/compliance.
- Shared services: S3-compatible object storage (private endpoint), metrics/ops endpoints (Prometheus push gateway, log sinks) and our health-checking LB.
- Egress patterns: we want to avoid customer hairpinning and double NAT. Proposal: per-datacenter egress proxy (customer-owned) + optional Redwood-managed egress IPs if the customer requires allowlisting.

Please review diagrams for any obvious gaps (routing, NAT, ports) and propose a short list of peering/handshake options you prefer (VGW/VPC peering/Transit GW, or direct physical peering).

Would like to get alignment this week and lock the network acceptance checklist before we start the Terraform automation. Proposed meeting: Wed 4/20 10:30 PT — ok?

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the diagram. Quick notes from our network team after an initial skim:

- Transit approach: for multi-AZ/datacenter customers we prefer a Transit Gateway (or equivalent) in front of the inference VPCs and a dedicated Transit VPC for shared services. Transit GW simplifies route propagation and avoids complex peering meshes.
- Control plane connectivity: mutual TLS over a long-lived GRE/IPSec tunnel is OK, but for latency-sensitive control signals consider TCP keepalives and a small MTU to reduce fragmentation if the customer's WAN uses MPLS.
- Egress: recommend customer-owned central egress proxies in each colo/rack cluster with explicit SNAT. If Atlas insists on Redwood-managed egress IPs for allowlists, we'll propose a small CIDR block and NAT gateway fleet.
- Security appliance: if the customer runs SNI inspection or a firewall, ensure the control-plane traffic uses a dedicated SNI hostname and certificate to avoid collateral blocking.

Questions:
1) Do you plan to rely on any public IP callback from the data plane for metrics or will all observability push through private endpoints?
2) Do you have an initial list of ports/protocols for the GPU nodes (we can standardize the ACL templates).

I've attached a short doc with peering options and tradeoffs. Happy to review live on 4/20.

--
Samir Patel

Thanks Samir — very helpful. Short answers to your questions and proposed decisions:

- Observability: Atlas prefers push-model for logs/metrics into their private sinks over a private endpoint. Redwood will support both: we can push telemetry to Atlas's Prometheus/PushGateway over the private link, or we can push to a Redwood-managed collector that then forwards in a single TLS stream. For now plan for private push to avoid public callbacks.
- Ports/protocols: initial ACL template below (Markus, please validate):
  - 443 (TLS) control-plane mTLS
  - 9411/9xxx (metrics/logs) over TLS to internal endpoints
  - 22 (ops) limited to jump hosts only
  - gRPC ports for model serving (we'll standardize in next doc)

Decisions/proposals:
1) Control plane: persistent mTLS from customer VPC to Redwood control-plane IPs; use mutual certs; Redwood provides a short allowlist (we'll own the cert rotation flow).
2) Data plane: runs inside customer VPC; egress via customer central proxy cluster. If Atlas will not supply a proxy, Redwood can provide managed egress IPs (small CIDR) as a fallback.
3) Routing: use Transit GW pattern where Atlas supports it; otherwise per-VPC peering with explicit route tables.
4) Automation: repo with Terraform modules (network + peering + cert bootstrap) — Priyom to draft.

Action items:
- Priyom: draft TF module skeleton and provide initial state variables (due 4/23).
- Markus: validate ACL template and provide specific gRPC port range (due 4/22).
- Laura: confirm Atlas's compliance requirement for egress IPs (due 4/21) and whether any traffic needs to be inspected by their DLP.
- Samir/Maya: share any firewall appliance constraints or SNI inspection requirements.

Meeting confirmed: 4/20 10:30 PT (we'll use the attached doc as the discussion guide).

Thanks,
Jonas

Folks — pulling together a short technical checklist and implementation notes:

Network/CIDR placeholders (for Atlas to confirm):
- Control plane allowlist (Redwood-managed fallback): 34.82.10.0/24, 34.82.11.0/24
- Observability collector endpoint (private): 10.200.50.10:443 (customer-owned)
- Managed egress NAT pool (if requested): 34.82.12.0/28
Routing/peering notes:
- Prefer Transit GW when Atlas runs multiple VPCs across AZs; it simplifies propagation. If on-prem with BGP, prefer BGP with MD5 auth and route filtering.
- Avoid hairpinning: ensure that egress proxy routes are injected at the VPC edge and not through a second NAT hop.
Security & certs:
- mTLS: use mutual certs with short TTL; integrate cert rotation with customer KMS where possible.
- HSM/KMS: call out if Atlas needs to store model keys on their HSM. We'll provide integration hooks in the private deployment package.

Ports & ACL starting template:
- 443/tcp (mTLS control-plane)
- 9411/tcp (metrics over TLS)
- 22/tcp (ops jump hosts) — restricted to jump host CIDRs only
- 12000-12100/tcp (model gRPC serving — exact range TBD)

Operational checklist for handoff:
1) Confirm Atlas CIDR allocations and whether they will host central proxies.
2) Provide allowed firewall appliance rules and SNI inspection policies (if any).
3) Exchange cert signing details and bootstrapping process.
4) Run a dry Terraform plan in a staging VPC (Priyom to own).

I'll populate a concrete Terraform variable file once Atlas confirms CIDRs.
